content.title: About
content.content: Flan is a smooth custard dessert made from eggs, milk, sugar, and flavorings (most often vanilla). Its texture is silky and slightly wobbly, and the taste is sweet and creamy. The dessert is usually served chilled, sometimes with a caramel sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flan has Spanish origins; the word “flan” comes from the Latin “flado,” meaning “flat cake.”
Different countries add their own twists: Mexico often uses cinnamon and clove, while Japan may incorporate sweet soy sauce.
Traditional serving is in small ceramic ramekins that are inverted to let the caramel flow over the sides.
Flan is frequently offered in restaurants as a light finish to a meal because it isn’t overly heavy.
There is a coconut‑milk version popular among vegetarians and those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs, the main ingredient, provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Milk supplies calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D from dairy aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low‑fat option with skim milk
items.content: Using skim milk makes flan a lighter dessert with reduced fat content.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture and simple ingredients make flan gentle on the stomach.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: Flan contains eggs and milk, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional flan is sweet; people monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its light texture, flan can be calorie‑rich due to sugar and milk fats.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: If left at room temperature too long, bacteria can grow in flan.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Flan is served chilled, often drizzled with caramel, topped with berries, fruit puree, or a sprinkle of ground cinnamon. It can be eaten directly from the ramekin with a spoon or transferred to a plate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store finished flan in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 3‑4 days. Chill for at least 2 hours before serving. Do not leave flan at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
